summary: Startup-critical scheduler and worker hotpoint exchange actions now use RuntimeController atomic admission, and the STARTING dashboard gate rejects every registered origin. Other dashboard placement paths still rely on an optimistic handler check followed by plain or untracked REST work, so a post-start pause race and one uniform repository-wide admission boundary remain unproven.

StealthOrderBridge.record_reveal_event calls _save_reveal_event_to_db, but that method is pass. Accepted reveal history is independently persisted by StealthOrderManager, so the bridge persistence path is dead/non-authoritative.

Ticker bridge stores volume_1m, while CumulativeVolumeEvaluator reads trade_volume; manager also constructs a new evaluator on every condition check, discarding evaluator-owned volume buckets. The cumulative-volume condition cannot accumulate through this runtime path.

The unmanaged cancel_order fallback still passes client_order_id to raw cancel_orders(order_ids=[...]), so its exchange identifier contract remains unproven. Managed stealth roots and placement IDs now route through the canonical logical-stop path, which cancels the tracked exchange order_id and preserves recovery state.

WebSocket position snapshots update OrderBook memory, while the OrderEngine dashboard-position helper has no statically resolved production caller. Live/hydrated positions are therefore not proven to enter dashboard engine_state.

Authenticated ingress and keyed lifecycle dispatch are bounded and fail closed without partial envelope admission. Ticker overflow retains the newest envelope and propagates continuity loss. Other non-ticker public ingress still claims EventBridge deduplication before bounded insertion and does not release that claim on queue.Full, so those public channels have no retry.

Event-stream coverage is hook-path dependent: repeated same-status idempotency keys can collapse events, UPDATE is not a registered status hook, and dashboard/hotpoint placement paths do not necessarily enter the stealth placement hook route.

evidence.anchor: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS order_parent

summary: Unknown-order externally_created provenance exists only in the in-memory parent cache and is absent from order_parent. The periodic snapshot replaces parent maps with DB-shaped rows, after which _is_external_order can default that known parent to local without an explicit adoption event.

Private heartbeat envelopes participate in connection-global sequence validation and are then intentional no-ops; public heartbeat events are also dequeued without business processing. The project does not inspect heartbeat_counter as a second continuity signal.

evidence.anchor: Websocket trigger for user message events.

summary: data.StateManager and websocket/on_message/user.py plus websocket/ticker.py have no statically resolved ownership from main.py and appear to be parallel/dormant state or re-export surfaces; do not choose them as production edit points without dynamic proof.

evidence.anchor: Hooks execute after the DB write

summary: Lifecycle hook documentation describes after-DB, separate-connection, nonblocking behavior, but callbacks are synchronous and reveal lifecycle dispatch can precede stealth/reveal persistence while OrderEventStreamPublisher uses the shared database module.

The v2 OrderBook has its own lock, the compatibility shim exposes live dictionaries, and OrderEngine uses a second orderbook_lock. The repository has no single mechanically enforced lock domain for all access to the same underlying state.

No single durable ownership source exists: external/local classification uses volatile cache provenance, stealth placement ownership uses _placed_order_index, fill reconciliation infers mappings from order_event_stream, and startup reconciliation treats nonterminal order_parent rows as local.

get_parent_orders returns every order_parent row, and build_parent_child_order_ids_snapshot treats each as a root while deriving children only from stealth_orders. A placement/follow-up row can be classified as a root or simultaneously as root and child.

evidence.anchor: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS partial_fill_progress

summary: OrderProgressTracker uses last_filled_value, last_total_fees, and snapshot_seq, but partial_fill_progress neither stores nor hydrates them from durable columns. Restart can replay historical value/fee deltas and restart snapshot numbering.

Historical pause ambiguity is resolved for scheduler-owned anchor actions: admission and in-flight registration now share the RuntimeController state-lock boundary. Pause either wins first and the due work is rebuilt without manager execution, or the action was already admitted/tracked and may finish as existing in-flight work; no action is newly admitted after pause wins.

The scheduler reveal path closes the historical pause race by atomically checking admission and registering inflight work. If pause wins first, reveal is deferred with TRIGGERED state retained and no recurring retry; the next admission-open edge publishes one immediate wake. Otherwise the already-admitted reveal may finish as existing inflight work.

evidence.anchor: Measured pre-correction boundary from the stateful run
The consumed wake and its replacement

summary: Guarded pre-correction instrumentation measured 844 schedules and 421 delivered wakes for one PAUSED TRIGGERED row in roughly 45 seconds because both evaluator and deadline handler published successors. The current correction removes non-admitting recurrence and generation-fences active successor ownership; deterministic tests replace this historical hazard with inv:stealth_admission_retry_ownership.

PostgresDB.get_cursor rolls back only psycopg2.Error. A non-psycopg2 exception raised by caller code inside the context exits through finally without explicit rollback, potentially leaving transaction state for the shared connection.

The monotonic progress watermark advances before several separate best-effort DB writes. A write failure followed by an identical event replay in the same process can be classified as no new delta and remain unpersisted.

evidence.anchor: Repricing and manual rehide do not place a replacement here.

summary: The automatic-anchor half of this former combined risk is resolved because revealed repricing and manual Rehide request cancellation through the shared rearm path without placing a replacement. Manual MOVE still continues to exchange placement after a local parent pre-insert error; exchange acceptance can therefore coexist with incomplete local finalization.

Reveal calls _pre_insert_placement_row but does not gate REST placement on its boolean return. An accepted venue order after local pre-insert failure enters local-finalization-error handling instead of being prevented.

The historical fully-revealed exposure-size bug is resolved. Automatic repricing now derives the live quantity from the accepted reveal event rather than remaining_size, validates it against current revealed inventory, persists a cancellation intent, and only matching zero-fill authenticated cancellation restores that quantity to HIDDEN. It neither clears active pointers nor places a replacement on the initial ticker path.

If authenticated cancellation carries fill evidence while a revealed rearm (automatic reprice or manual Rehide) is pending, the safety path aborts rearming, marks the whole logical stealth order CANCELLED with zero remaining size, and pauses. It intentionally does not return an unfilled residual to HIDDEN; whether that residual should continue is an unresolved product policy rather than an implemented behavior.

A fresh/reset database is not fully hydrated by normal main.py startup: current component initializers create only subsets, leaving core tables such as order_parent/order_moves/stealth_order_moves/order_match_audit dependent on prior initialization.

The historical startup admission and shutdown-revival windows are closed: RuntimeController begins STARTING, passive hydration precedes dashboard exposure, registered dashboard origins and worker hotpoint placement are gated, and readiness follows reconciliation/scheduler/periodic/worker launch. Shutdown or partial startup requests bounded cooperative cleanup and cannot reopen admission; timeout may still leave recorded unfinished or daemon work exiting.

Stealth reconciliation adds only missing active IDs and publishes their schedules, but it does not refresh or evict existing cached rows. Structural cache insertion is locked, while database discovery, insertion and bridge schedule publication are not one atomic manager-wide transaction.

evidence.anchor: Direct cancellation left the paired root

summary: Local-only pre-reveal cancellation persists the stealth stop but still leaves its same-SID order_parent projection PENDING and omits the CANCELLED lifecycle event. Dashboard responses now honor the manager outcome and distinguish pending exchange withdrawal. Live tracked placements defer pointer and parent completion to authenticated cancellation; that correction does not repair the remaining local-only parent projection drift.

The former best-effort direct-cancel pointer-loss hazard is resolved for the bounded tracked-placement path. Project cancellation now persists the logical stop and terminal recovery intent before REST, retains exposure identifiers on rejection/timeout, and clears them only after authenticated terminal truth. Incomplete identity or unaccounted multi-placement exposure stops automation and pauses for reconciliation without pretending withdrawal succeeded.

ticker_lock is held across dashboard, database, metrics, and bridge work; due revealed anchor repricing can synchronously persist intent and request exchange cancellation. Slow database or cancel I/O can therefore block ticker cache progress, although replacement placement now belongs to a later reveal cycle rather than this critical section.
The historical PATCH drop is closed: PATCH remains a distinct wire kind and complete post-bootstrap PATCH rows enter the same canonical live dispatcher as UPDATE.

The private WSUserClient now has an engine-owned reconnect loop and generation reset. Redundant public WSClient recovery still relies on the Coinbase SDK's internal retry behavior rather than an engine outer loop.

The approved snapshot hydration remains intentionally narrow: it returns for an empty venue set, does not evict in-memory OPEN rows absent from Coinbase, and no-ops rows whose status matches even when quantities changed. Drift is reported, but absence and same-status field correction are not fully self-healing.

The historical per-page hydration conflict is closed: one generation accumulates 50-row snapshot/PATCH/UPDATE pages until the first short page, then performs one drift check and one in-memory hydration without bootstrap lifecycle side effects.

The historical duplicate-private-subscription conflict is closed: public market data retains configured redundant WSClient fan-out while all authenticated payload channels share one WSUserClient thread.
